subject: Renewal + mid-contract uplift: proposed quota repack for Acme AI
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@acme.ai>
Cc: Ben Zhao <ben.zhao@acme.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal + mid-contract uplift: proposed quota repack for Acme AI

Hi Samira,

Quick note following our call this morning — really appreciate the context on the Q2 pilots ramping faster than expected. Based on the growth you described, I put together two pragmatic options to cover your uplift without forcing a full annual reset: one staggered top-up (credit-style) and one co-term reprice that annualizes the incremental commitment.

I attached v1 of the quote with both options and an estimated cost delta vs current run-rate. High-level:
- Option A: Staged top-up (3-month bridge + credit) — preserves existing term and spreads invoice impact.
- Option B: Co-term + annualize incremental commit — slightly larger discount in exchange for a catch-up commit through next renewal.

Can you confirm which path Procurement prefers (spread vs co-term)? If neither, tell me your preferred budget/target uplift and I’ll reshape.

Next step: if you’re open, I’ll loop in Naomi (CS) and Priyom (commercial) for technical and billing alignment and share a v2 that includes invoice timing.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0198
[attachment: ACME-Renewal-Quote-v1.pdf]

From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@acme.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Zhao <ben.zhao@acme.ai>, procure@acme.ai
Date: Tue, 3 Apr 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal + mid-contract uplift: proposed quota repack for Acme AI

Karthik — thanks for sending. I reviewed the attachment with Ben and Procurement. Two quick constraints from our side:
1) Budget window: Q2 has a fixed remaining budget; we cannot absorb a large one-time invoice this quarter.
2) Approval cadence: any >$200k net-new spend requires VP procurement sign-off and legal review, which slows things down.

Prefer Option A (staged top-up) but need the monthly invoice to be < $65k and the total uplift spread across at least 3 invoice cycles. Also need confirmation that usage above the top-up bucket will still allow safe fallback to the hosted tier without throttles.

Can you propose a 3-invoice schedule that keeps each invoice <= $65k and includes an SLA addendum for fallback behaviour?

Best,
Samira
Head of Platform | Acme AI
[sent from mobile]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Apr 2028 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Renewal + mid-contract uplift: proposed quota repack for Acme AI

Team — forwarding Acme’s note. They prefer the staged top-up but capped monthly invoice <= $65k and want an explicit fallback assurance for consumption above the top-up.

Naomi: can you confirm the technical fallback and whether we can guarantee seamless fallback to hosted variant within SLA window (they want an addendum language).
Priyom: need pricing help to slice the uplift into 3 invoices that meet the $65k cap and keep our margin intact. Laura: heads up in case VP-level approval gets required.

I attached v1 — I’ll draft v2 with the split once we have a pricing thumb.

— Karthik
[attachment: ACME-Renewal-Quote-v1.pdf]

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Apr 2028 08:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal + mid-contract uplift: proposed quota repack for Acme AI

Karthik — quick technical note: we can implement a soft fallback that routes to a hosted variant with identical model family but lower reserved capacity. We can commit to a 10s tail-latency SLO for fallback initiation (i.e., detection + route), but cannot guarantee identical throughput under sustained exceed (they’ll experience degraded throughput until additional capacity is applied). I can draft clause language: detection threshold, fallback behaviour, and a 30-day remediation window for permanent capacity adjustments.

I’ll also provide a short runbook for Acme’s SREs to tune client-side retry/backoff to avoid alert storms during a fallback.

Naomi
Customer Success | Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.ai

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 5 Apr 2028 10:16:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing split for Acme staged top-up

Karthik / Team — ran numbers and modeled three invoice splits that keep per-invoice at or below $65k while preserving a blended uplift discount similar to our v1. Key assumptions: 12-month blended ARR on new uplift, 15% uplift discount for the co-term style but we’re structuring this as credit-style spread (Option A) so discount is 8% effective.

Proposed split (v2):
- Invoice 1 (May): $64,950 — applies 40% of uplift units
- Invoice 2 (Jun): $64,950 — applies 35% of uplift units
- Invoice 3 (Jul): $64,950 — applies remaining 25% + prorated license smoothing

Net impact vs v1: total net uplift = $194,850 (3-invoice sum), we keep a modest commercial concession to account for operational switching (8% effective). I attached v2 that shows unit math and the invoice schedule.

If Procurement asks for lower per-invoice cap, we could stretch to 4 invoices but that erodes margin; recommend pushing for 3.

Priyom
Senior Commercial Ops | Redwood Inference
[attachment: ACME-Renewal-Quote-v2.pdf]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@acme.ai>
Cc: Ben Zhao <ben.zhao@acme.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal + mid-contract uplift: proposed quota repack for Acme AI

Samira — thanks for the quick turn. Per your ask we prepared v2 with a 3-invoice structure that keeps each invoice at $64,950 and includes proposed fallback language and the SRE runbook. See the attachments.

Summary:
- 3 invoices: May / Jun / Jul @ $64,950 each (total $194,850).
- Fallback addendum: soft routing to a hosted-compatible variant; detection + route <= 10s; 30-day remediation for sustained capacity shortages (see legal-friendly clause in attached PDF).
- We will not throttle active requests; instead fallback will route requests to the hosted variant and surface metrics so Acme can measure degraded throughput.

If that works, I’ll kick off an updated quote (v3) and Docusign envelope for a signature path that only requires Procurement sign-off (no VP exec) given the < $200k total.

Next step: Confirm by EOD Thursday and I’ll send the v3/docuSign.

— Karthik
[attachment: ACME-Renewal-Quote-v3.pdf]
